---- Transcript ----
00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, this is maya se and connor on the call with me, we'll do a quick intro then dig into integration patterns for sdk + gateway.
00:18 Jordan: great thanks, we are looking at replacing a homegrown proxy that talks to openai and replicate, want something with more predictable cost and enterprise controls.
00:34 Maya: perfect, why don't you give us a quick sense of current flow - where are calls originating, what are your throughput and latency expectations?
00:48 Priya: sure, most traffic starts in our checkout microservice in k8s, average payload per request is small (~200 tokens) but peak spikes during sales events up to ~500 rps. 95th pct latency goal is sub-150ms for embeddings and sub-300ms for generation when in-hosted path.
01:12 Ethan: also want to note we have strict egress rules, all external API calls have to go through our gateway/proxy or through a VPC endpoint, and we need audit logs.
01:31 Alex: ok makes sense - so three model of interest for you: Redwood Hosted for quick POC, Redwood Dedicated reserved pools if you want predictable throughput, and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need full network isolation. Any initial leaning?
01:47 Jordan: leaning hosted for speed to market but want to validate latency during peak. if hosted can't meet SLO we'll look dedicated. private is likely only for regulatory customers.
02:05 Maya: on SDKs - we have official SDKs for node/python, and connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. for teams doing retrieval-augmented generation we often show the langchain example and a LlamaIndex adapter. do you use those already?
02:20 Priya: we've got langchain in a couple services, but our embeddings code is custom. curious how seamless switching provider is.
02:33 Connor: generally it is a few config changes - our SDK supports the same call shapes as openai-ish APIs plus a compatibility layer for langchain and llamaindex. we also publish example notebooks and a small repo that demonstrates switching providers with minimal changes. i'll share the link after the call.
02:51 Jordan: good, also about gateway/proxy - if we route through our internal gateway, do you have IP allowlists or do we need to open wider egress?
03:05 Maya: for hosted we allow IP ranges and can set up customer-specific whitelists; for private we bring the control plane into your VPC. for dedicated we can also support VPC peering or private link depending on region. there are tradeoffs on management overhead.
03:24 Lena: encryption and KMS - we want envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for certain datasets. how do you handle KMS and audit logs?
03:36 Alex: we support KMS integrations for private/dedicated and for hosted we can enable CMEK for enterprise customers; audit logs for all requests available in Redwood Console with retention tiers as an add-on. we'll send SOC2 docs you can hand to compliance.
03:56 Priya: great. on rate limits - what's the standard quota model and can we request higher burst capacity during promotions?
04:08 Maya: hosted has per-account quotas and per-key rate limits; you can apply for higher quotas and we have burst policies. dedicated gives you reserved capacity with predictable throughput and can be configured to autoscale within policy. we also support token-level throttling and customer-configurable queueing.
04:31 Ethan: will that play nicely with our retry logic? we typically do exponential backoff but want to avoid long tails under retry storms.
04:41 Connor: yes - we recommend idempotency keys for important calls and circuit-breaker patterns at the gateway. Redwood Console can surface per-route error and latency spikes so you can tune retry windows.
04:59 Jordan: anything special for embeddings? we have a vector DB and want consistent embeddings across runs, also 0-drift when moving providers.
05:12 Maya: we have model version pinning so you can lock to a model/quantization profile. for high-consistency you can use our dedicated pools with fixed model variants. small caveat: different model families will have inherent shifts - we can run a calibration dataset in the POC to measure drift.
05:37 Priya: awesome. about observability - can we hook tracing into our existing datadog/jaeger?
05:46 Connor: yes, Redwood Console exposes tracing hooks and we emit spans that can be forwarded to vendor endpoints. we also have webhooks and a logs exporter. sometimes the auto-transcription mislabels spans but raw request metadata and token-level timing is available.
06:06 Jordan: that covers most questions, can we talk about real integration work - use of SDK, langchain glue, and a simple proxy architecture?
06:18 Maya: sure, typical integration: your checkout service calls our node SDK, which handles auth and retry. if you use langchain, you swap in Redwood as a provider in the chain. alternatively, you can centralize calls through your gateway/proxy so traffic originates from a small set of IPs and you can apply rate-limiting and observability there.
06:38 Priya: our team prefers to centralize via the gateway for security reasons. is there a recommended pattern to avoid double-queuing if gateway also does throttling?
06:49 Connor: put the gateway as a thin pass-through with rate-limiter tokens and let Redwood handle per-key throttling; gateway should propagate request metadata and idempotency header so Redwood Console can correlate.
07:06 Ethan: any setup needed to get SDK keys into our secrets manager? will the SDK rotate keys automatically?
07:16 Alex: we support short-lived tokens, and you can integrate with your secret store. for dedicated/private there's more control: service accounts, KMS-backed keys, and audit trails.
07:28 Jordan: talk to me about cost - we need a baseline comparison of hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved costs for our throughput.
07:36 Maya: we'll send a pricing worksheet; typically at your scale with 500 rps peaks, dedicated becomes cost-effective when you have steady high throughput. we can model a few traffic shapes in the POC.
07:51 Jordan: POC plan?
07:54 Alex: propose a 2-week POC: week 1 run Redwood Hosted against your traffic replay to validate latency and correctness; week 2 run a dedicated trial (short reserved pool) to compare throughput and unit cost. we can help run benchmarks and provide a small script to replay traffic.
08:14 Priya: do you need any infra access for the POC?
08:19 Maya: for hosted we just need API keys and traffic samples; for dedicated you can spin up a test VPC or we can run in a shared regional pool depending on timeline. for private deployments we'll need more ops coordination.
08:36 Jordan: security questions - SSO for team access, RBAC, and audit logs - how mature are those features?
08:46 Alex: SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC in the Console, and per-token access logs are supported. for enterprise we can add longer audit retention and forward logs to your storage.
08:59 Lena: are there known limitations with our k8s setup? our pods have egress restrictions and we use NAT gateways.
09:10 Connor: hosted will require opening outbound to the listed IP ranges or using a proxy; dedicated/private can be peered. we'll document the exact network ports and recommendations.
09:26 Jordan: ok, about langchain/llamaindex - do you provide vector store integrations?
09:34 Maya: yes, we have adapters for common vector DBs and patterns for doing chunking and embeddings. our sample repos show how to plug in LlamaIndex too; sometimes the transcribed example uses 'llama in dex' - spelled weirdly in the auto notes.
09:52 Priya: we use pinecone currently, will that be straightforward?
09:58 Connor: yes, embeddings compatible. we'll share a sample flow: Redwood embeddings -> pinecone upsert -> langchain retrieval.
10:08 Jordan: latency for embeddings at 200 tokens - will that consistently be under 150ms?
10:16 Maya: hosted typically averages around 80-120ms depending on region; dedicated can be tuned for lower tail latency. we also do KV cache prefix caching for repeated prompts which helps. note that network egress and your NAT latency adds to the total.
10:37 Ethan: how does token counting and billing work with batching enabled?
10:43 Alex: billing is per-token; with batching you get throughput improvements but billing still counts the underlying tokens. our billing reports show token-level breakdowns per-route so you can attribute cost.
10:55 Jordan: any gotchas when moving from hosted to dedicated? model versions, quantization changes, that sort of thing?
11:05 Maya: main thing is to pin model versions and quantization profile. also, we may use different kernels under dedicated which can slightly change token timing but not output semantics in most cases. we'll run regressions in POC.
11:22 Priya: ok will you share the SDK quickstart and langchain example?
11:27 Alex: yes - maya will share links.
11:30 Maya: i'll drop the examples and a litle notebook showing the switch. also include a small traffic replay script.
11:38 Jordan: what about rate limiting during promo spikes - can you do burst credit?
11:44 Maya: yes, we have burst capacity options for hosted and dedicated - dedicated gives explicit reserved CPU/GPU capacity so bursts are smoother.
11:52 Ethan: observability hooks - we'd like token-level timing exported to datadog, and an alert if 95th latency crosses 250ms. is that doable?
12:03 Connor: yes, alerts can be configured in Redwood Console or you can forward metrics to datadog. we can create a sample dashboard and an alert playbook.
12:14 Jordan: any compliance red flags we should know about?
12:18 Alex: none obvious. we'll share SOC2 and encryption docs. for regulated data we recommend private deployment with customer-managed keys.
12:30 Priya: timeline - assuming POC goes well, how long to stand up dedicated?
12:37 Maya: depends on region and capacity - usually 2-4 weeks to provision dedicated pools with testing; private on-prem longer.
12:46 Jordan: ok let's recap next steps.
12:50 Alex: recap - we'll: 1) send Dedicated pricing worksheet and hosted cost model, 2) share SDK + LangChain + LlamaIndex examples, 3) provide security docs (SOC2, KMS), 4) propose 2-week POC plan and a traffic replay script.
13:13 Jordan: sounds good, i'll gather the spike traffic and sample SLOs and get back by monday.
13:20 Priya: i'll collect the sample logs and share the traffic profile.
13:24 Alex: we'll follow up with an invite for technical deep-dive next week with your infra team. thanks everyone.
13:31 Jordan: thanks all.
